findings.title: TableWidgetVisualization rendered with hardcoded empty data
findings.body: In the new `use-table-widget-visualization` feature branch, `TableWidgetVisualization` is mounted with `columns={[]}` and `tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}` — the actual `result.data` and `result.meta` produced by the dataset query (and used by the legacy `StyledSimpleTableChart` below) are discarded. Any organization that enables the `use-table-widget-visualization` flag will see fully empty tables in every dashboard table widget regardless of query results. To wire the data correctly, the component must receive the per-result columns/fields and the real `result.data`/`result.meta`, e.g. by deriving columns from `datasetConfig.getFieldHeaderMap?.(widget.queries[i])` and the fields list, and passing `tableData={{data: result.data, meta: result.meta}}`.

findings.title: fetch_error_details pairs nodestore results assuming order preservation
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` calls `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` and then does `for event_id, data in zip(error_ids, events.values()):`, which only produces the correct (event_id, event_data) pairs if `get_multi` returns values in the same order as the requested keys. Some nodestore backends (e.g. concurrent/Nydus-style backends) do not guarantee that, so when more than one error is fetched the AI summary can receive mismatched titles/messages/timestamps for different events. The code should key the lookup by node_id (`events[node_id]`) rather than relying on the order of `events.values()`.

findings.title: Replays AI summary no longer honors ?project= URL override
findings.body: The component previously obtained the project via `useLocationQuery({fields: {project: decodeScalar}})`, allowing the `?project=<id>` query parameter to choose a different project than the one stored on the replay (commonly used for cross-project replays or admin-impersonated views). The change drops that hook and now uses `useProjectFromId({project_id: replayRecord?.project_id})`, so any caller navigating to this view with `?project=...` will silently get the replay's stored project instead of the requested one, and the API call to `/projects/${slug}/replays/${id}/summarize/breadcrumbs/` may target the wrong project (404 or wrong data) or use the wrong feature flag check.

findings.title: get_environment_info hits nodestore for every issue
findings.body: `get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` for every issue included in the PR/MR comment. That helper performs a nodestore lookup (`Event.objects.get(id=...)`) per call. For a comment that lists N issues this produces N sequential nodestore round-trips on the hot path of PR comment generation, and each call is wrapped in a broad `except Exception` that swallows programming errors and only logs at info level. Consider caching the recommended event per group, batching lookups, or limiting the lookup to cases where an environment field is actually useful.

findings.title: dcg_to_slow_conditions built from dcg_ids instead of dcg_to_groups.keys()
findings.body: Previously `get_condition_query_groups` computed `dcg_to_slow_conditions = get_slow_conditions_for_groups(list(event_data.dcg_to_groups.keys()))` while `fetch_data_condition_groups` was fed `event_data.dcg_ids`. After the refactor both consume `event_data.dcg_ids`. If `EventRedisData.dcg_to_groups` and `dcg_ids` ever contain different sets (e.g. one includes a DCG that the other omits), `dcg_to_slow_conditions` will look up a stale or missing entry and the `KeyError` path or `slow_conditions` could be wrong. Either confirm the two sets are always equal (and add a guard) or pass the key set that actually drives `data_condition_groups`.
